title: The incentre of the centre-cut pyramid: rigidity of the truncated n-cubic contact framework, a radius-ratio identity, and the CaB6 packing maximum
description: Cut an n-cube into the 2n pyramids that join its centre to its facets and place a ball at the incentre of each pyramid. The centres are the Wythoff points of the [4,3^(n-2),4] kaleidoscope. We prove that at a generic wavevector the contact framework has exactly n(n-1)/2 zero modes and n(n-3)/2 states of self-stress per cell, and that with unit springs every shear modulus vanishes and the Poisson ratio is 1/(n^2-n-1). We also record a radius-ratio identity, the closed form (pi/6)(30 sqrt2 - 41) for the maximal packing fraction of the CaB6 structure type, and a verified bar-preserving, overlap-free fold of the three-dimensional framework to hexagonal and face-centred cubic close packing. The archive contains the preprint, the interactive site, replayable verifiers and certificates. Not peer reviewed.
notes: Computation, proofs, checking and writing were carried out with AI assistance (Claude Opus 5.5 and other Claude models from Anthropic) under the author's direction; see CONTRIBUTORS.md.
